paper_metadata.title: Unsupervised quantum machine learning for fraud detection

experiments.description: Supervised quantum fraud classification using a quantum kernel SVM on a credit card fraud dataset, evaluated across increasing numbers of PCA features/qubits with an IQP-style feature map and re-uploading.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel support vector classification with IQP feature map and data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: IQP-like feature map with Hadamard layer, feature-dependent rotations, ZZ entangling gates, repeated twice per IQP layer and re-uploaded d = 3 times

hyperparameters.pca_features: varied from small N up to 20

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One feature per qubit; PCA-reduced and standardized features are scaled by eta = 0.1 before being embedded into x-dependent single-qubit rotations and pairwise ZZ phases.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Supervised binary classification of fraudulent vs genuine transactions using a kernel SVM decision function.

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on a subsampled public benchmark dataset, using supervised labels for evaluation.

dataset_specification.description: Original dataset has 284,807 transactions and 492 fraud cases; paper uses 500 samples including 25 fraud cases for visualization and benchmarking, and applies standard scaling followed by PCA, keeping the first N principal components. Only the 28 anonymized features are used; time and amount are excluded.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature-wise standard scaling, PCA dimensionality reduction, feature rescaling by eta = 0.1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average precision computed from predicted scores.

experiments.description: Unsupervised fraud anomaly detection using classical one-class SVM with RBF kernel as the baseline for comparison to quantum kernels.

algorithm.variant: One-class SVM with classical RBF kernel

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical PCA-reduced feature vectors are used directly; only nominal data are used to fit the OC-SVM.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Novelty detection / anomaly detection by separating nominal points from outliers with a one-class SVM decision boundary.

problem_instance.description: Unsupervised anomaly detection on the same credit card fraud dataset, using only nominal samples for training and evaluating average precision against fraud labels.

dataset_specification.description: Subsampled to 500 samples with 25 fraud cases; PCA applied after standard scaling; number of retained principal components varied with N.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature-wise standard scaling and PCA; only nominal transactions used for training.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average precision computed using fraud labels only for evaluation.

experiments.description: Quantum anomaly detection using an IQP quantum kernel inside one-class SVM, evaluated across increasing feature/qubit counts up to 20 qubits.

algorithm.variant: One-class SVM with IQP quantum kernel
algorithm.ansatz: IQP-like feature map with Hadamards, x-dependent rotations, ZZ entanglers, repeated twice per layer and re-uploaded d = 3 times

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each retained PCA feature is mapped to one qubit; features are scaled by eta = 0.1 to keep phases below 2π.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Unsupervised novelty detection with OC-SVM using quantum kernel overlaps κ(x,x') = |<ψ(x)|ψ(x')>|^2.

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud anomaly detection with PCA-preprocessed public benchmark data, using only nominal data for training and fraud labels for AP evaluation.

dataset_specification.description: 500-sample subsample with 25 fraud cases; standard scaling and PCA; feature count varied to match qubit count.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature-wise standard scaling, PCA, and rescaling by eta = 0.1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average precision from anomaly scores; Gram matrix assembled from quantum kernel evaluations.

experiments.description: Quantum supervised classification benchmark using the same IQP quantum kernel, compared against classical supervised baselines across feature sizes up to 20 qubits.

algorithm.ansatz: IQP-like feature map with re-uploading d = 3

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per feature after PCA reduction; data scaled by eta = 0.1.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of fraud vs genuine transactions using a quantum kernel SVM.

problem_instance.description: Supervised fraud classification on the same public credit card dataset, with performance tracked as the number of features/qubits increases.

dataset_specification.description: Subsampled 500-point dataset with 25 fraud cases; PCA and standard scaling applied; evaluation shown for increasing N.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Standard scaling, PCA, feature rescaling by eta = 0.1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average precision computed from classification scores.

experiments.description: Resource and feasibility analysis for deploying the quantum-kernel fraud detection workflow on near- and mid-term hardware platforms, including superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic systems.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel evaluation resource estimation for fraud detection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same one-feature-per-qubit quantum kernel encoding as above; resource estimates are based on Gram-matrix evaluation for pairwise overlaps.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate training and inference time for quantum-kernel-based fraud detection.

problem_instance.description: Scalability and hardware feasibility study for the fraud-detection workflow, using the reduced 500-sample dataset and an industrial-scale 100,000-sample scenario.

dataset_specification.description: Resource estimates are given for the reduced experimental dataset and for a hypothetical large dataset of about 100,000 samples.

speedup_claims.factor: O(N_s^2) kernel evaluations for full Gram matrix training; O(N_d N_s) for inference; O(N_s) with randomized/adaptive partial inference
speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum-kernel fraud detection training and inference on datasets of size N_s and N_d new samples
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-scaling analysis, not an empirical runtime benchmark; the linear-scaling claim requires randomized protocols and adaptive detection.

speedup_claims.factor: MHz-rate superconducting hardware could train the reduced 500-sample dataset in about 100 s with 10^3 shots; full 100,000-sample training could take 16 weeks
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming superconducting circuits, 10^3 shots, and optimistic MHz repetition
speedup_claims.caveats: Estimates depend strongly on shot count and hardware repetition rate.

speedup_claims.factor: trapped-ion reduced-dataset training about 3 hours; large-dataset brute-force training about 30 years at 10 kHz and 10^3 shots
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming 10 kHz absolute rate and 10^3 shots
speedup_claims.caveats: Large-dataset estimate is infeasible without sparse or parallel kernel evaluation.

speedup_claims.factor: photonic reduced-dataset training about 10 ms; large-dataset training about 17 minutes at 10^3 shots
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming 100 ps gate/lifetime scale and 10^3 shots
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that deterministic optical gates are not yet established.

scalability_data.metric_value: full Gram matrix becomes extremely costly
